input.title: Handle prefix in exp treatements by new endpoint
input.body:
## Problem
Experiments served by the new TAS assignments endpoint (`POST /api/v1/assignments`) were not being applied for some users, even though their `abexp.assignmentcontext` telemetry showed the experiment as assigned.

**Root cause:** the new endpoint namespaces the feature-variable keys it returns with a `/vscode/` scope (e.g. `/vscode/config.chat.copilot.subagentModelGuidance.enabled`), while VS Code core and the Copilot extension query treatments by the **bare** name (`config.chat...`). `tas-client` / `vscode-tas-client` store those keys verbatim under the `vscode` config, so `getTreatmentVariable('vscode', '<bare name>')` misses and returns `undefined`.

## Fix (interim, VS Code side)
Until the scope is stripped upstream `AssignmentsApiFeatureProvider.toFeatureData`, resolve treatments **scoped-first**: read the `/vscode/`-scoped key first, then fall back to the bare key.

- **Core** (`assignmentService.ts`): added a small pure helper `resolveScopedTreatment(read, name)` (scoped key first, bare fallback) and use it in `doGetTreatment`. Also simplified the pre-fetch handling into a single "await the initial fetch when not yet initialized" barrier and removed a redundant re-read.
- **Copilot extension** (`baseExperimentationService.ts`): centralized reads into `_readTreatmentVariable` (scoped-first, bare fallback), used by both `getTreatmentVariable` and the treatment-change detection so they stay consistent.

## Why scoped-first (new endpoint wins on collision)
This matches the behavior once the upstream strip lands: with the prefix removed, both endpoints produce the same bare key and the library merges them last-writer-wins in provider order (legacy registered first, assignments second → **new wins**). Making the interim shim scoped-first keeps the winner **consistent before and after** the upstream fix, so there's no behavior flip at cutover.


## Tests
- **Copilot** (`experimentation.spec.ts`): added cases for new-endpoint-only (scoped) resolution and collision (new wins); updated the suite mock so scoped lookups model "not assigned by the new endpoint," exercising the bare fallback.
- **Core** (`assignmentService.test.ts`): new unit tests for `resolveScopedTreatment` covering collision (new wins), legacy-only, new-only, neither, and a defined-falsy scoped value.
